experiences.name: Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim
experiences.description: Explore one of the Algarve's most stunning beaches, known for its dramatic golden limestone cliffs, sea caves, and crystal-clear turquoise waters. Hike the clifftop trail from Benagil and descend to the secluded cove for a refreshing swim and snorkeling among the rock formations.

experiences.name: Algarve Wine & Vineyard Tour
experiences.description: Visit local wineries in the Lagoa DOC wine region, the heart of Algarve winemaking. Tour the vineyards, learn about indigenous grape varieties like Negra Mole and Crato Branco, and enjoy guided tastings of crisp whites, rosés, and robust reds paired with local cheeses and charcuterie.

experiences.name: Benagil Sea Cave Kayak Tour
experiences.description: Paddle through the iconic Benagil Cave, one of the world's most photographed sea caves, accessible only by water. A guided kayak tour takes you through hidden grottos, arched rock formations, and secret beaches along the dramatic Algarve coastline, combining adventure with breathtaking natural beauty.

experiences.name: Sagres Sunset Cliffs & Local Seafood Dinner
experiences.description: Visit the windswept Cabo de São Vicente, the southwesternmost point of Europe, for a dramatic Atlantic sunset. Afterward, dine at a traditional tasca in Sagres village, savoring freshly grilled cataplana (seafood stew), percebes (barnacles), and local Algarve wine in an authentic fishing village atmosphere.
experiences.location: Sagres & Cabo de São Vicente, Vila do Bispo

experiences.name: Ria Formosa Natural Park Boat & Oyster Tasting
experiences.description: Take a guided boat tour through the Ria Formosa lagoon system, a protected natural park of tidal channels, barrier islands, and wildlife. Stop at a local oyster farm to taste freshly harvested oysters paired with chilled Algarve white wine, and explore the pristine barrier island beaches accessible only by boat.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Portugal Algarve
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Arrival day
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - Arrival day
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Faro Airport at 22:30 on flight UA. Take the Rede Expressos bus or Eva bus from Faro Airport to Lagos (approx. 1.5-2 hours, ~€6-8). Check in to Boutique Taghostel on Rua Dr. Faria e Silva, 32, Lagos. Drop off luggage and freshen up.

meals.breakfast: N/A
meals.lunch: N/A
meals.dinner: Grab a late-night snack at a nearby 24h convenience store or a kebab/pizza slice shop near the hostel in central Lagos (~€3-5)

day_by_day.notes: Keep your first night simple. The bus from Faro to Lagos is the most budget-friendly transfer option. Buy tickets at the Faro bus terminal just outside the airport arrivals hall. Last buses may run until midnight — confirm schedule in advance. Have hostel address saved offline.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. After a slow start, walk to Mercado de Lagos (Lagos Municipal Market) on Rua Lancarote de Freitas for a budget breakfast and to browse fresh local produce, cheeses, and pastries. Explore the historic old town of Lagos on foot — visit the Igreja de Santo António (free exterior, small fee inside ~€2) and the Slave Market Museum (Mercado de Escravos, ~€3).
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk 15 minutes south to Meia Praia or take a short stroll to Praia da Batata, a small sandy beach right at the edge of town. Relax, swim, and soak up the Algarve sun. The beach is free and easily walkable from the hostel.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Lagos marina and watch the sunset over the water. Head back into town for dinner on a budget.

meals.breakfast: Pastel de nata and coffee at Mercado de Lagos or a local pastelaria (~€2-3)
meals.lunch: Prego sandwich (steak roll) or bifana from a local tasca near the market (~€4-6)
meals.dinner: O Cantinho do Mar or a local tasca on Rua 25 de Abril — try grilled sardines or prato do dia (dish of the day) with bread, olives, and a glass of house wine (~€8-12)

day_by_day.notes: September is still warm and sunny in the Algarve — perfect beach weather. The old town of Lagos is very walkable from the hostel. Wear comfortable shoes for cobblestone streets.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning walk to Ponta da Piedade, one of the most iconic rock formations in the Algarve (~2km south of the hostel, free). Explore the clifftop viewpoints and dramatic golden limestone arches. Arrive early to avoid crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head down the steps to the small hidden beach at Ponta da Piedade. Alternatively, walk back toward town and visit Praia do Camilo, a stunning small beach tucked between cliffs (free, wooden staircase access). Spend the afternoon swimming and relaxing.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos town center. Browse the lively pedestrian streets around Rua 25 de Abril and Praça Gil Eanes. Enjoy a sundowner drink at a rooftop bar or a local cervejaria.

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and toast with butter and jam (torrada) at a local café near the hostel (~€2-3)
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic from the local supermarket (Lidl or Pingo Doce on Rua Portas de Portugal) — bread, local cheese, cured meats, fruit (~€4-5)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Adega da Marina near the marina — try cataplana de marisco (seafood stew) or grilled fish with potatoes (~€10-14)

day_by_day.notes: Ponta da Piedade is a must-see and completely free. The walk from the hostel takes about 25-30 minutes. Bring water and sunscreen. The steps down to the water can be slippery — wear grip shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Take a local bus (Eva/Rede Expressos) from Lagos bus station to Sagres (~45 min, ~€4 each way). Visit the dramatic Fortaleza de Sagres (Sagres Fortress) perched on a clifftop at the southwestern tip of Portugal (~€3 entry). Explore the windswept promontory and the famous wind compass (Rosa dos Ventos).
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short taxi to Praia do Beliche or Praia de Sagres — wild, uncrowded Atlantic beaches with powerful waves. Great for surfing or just watching the ocean. Explore the village of Sagres for local character.
day_by_day.evening: Return by bus to Lagos. Relax at the hostel and socialize with fellow travelers.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and pastel de nata at the hostel or a nearby café in Lagos before departure (~€2-3)
meals.lunch: A Tasca in Sagres village — fresh grilled fish or tuna steak with salad and local wine (~€9-12)
meals.dinner: Self-catering at the hostel — pick up ingredients from Pingo Doce supermarket in Lagos (~€5-7) or grab a cheap pizza slice from a local takeaway

day_by_day.notes: Sagres is the most southwestern point of continental Europe — a truly dramatic and windswept destination. Buses run several times daily from Lagos. Check the return schedule before you go. It can be windy even in September.

day_by_day.morning: Wine tasting day! Take a morning bus or arrange a shared taxi to Quinta dos Vales winery near Estômbar/Lagoa (~40 min from Lagos, bus to Portimão then local connection or taxi ~€15-20 shared). Quinta dos Vales offers affordable wine tours and tastings (~€10-15 per person) with beautiful sculpture gardens and vineyard views.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the wine tasting, head to nearby Portimão (bus from Lagoa, ~€2). Visit the Museu de Portimão (free on Sundays, otherwise ~€3) — a fascinating museum in a former fish canning factory. Walk along the Portimão riverfront promenade.
day_by_day.evening: Take the bus back to Lagos (~30 min, ~€3). Enjoy a relaxed evening in the hostel common area or explore Lagos nightlife on Rua 25 de Abril.

meals.breakfast: Yogurt, fruit, and coffee at the hostel or a local café (~€2-4)
meals.lunch: Light snacks and wine at the winery tasting (often included or available for purchase ~€5-8)
meals.dinner: Cervejaria Dois Irmãos in Portimão before heading back — grilled chicken or piri-piri prawns with fries (~€9-12)

day_by_day.notes: Book the winery tour in advance online to secure a spot and confirm pricing. Quinta dos Vales is one of the most accessible and affordable wineries in the Algarve. Alternatively, Adega do Cantor (Cliff Richard's winery) near Guia is another option but requires more planning.

day_by_day.morning: Take the bus to Portimão (~30 min, ~€3) and then a short ferry or walk to Praia da Rocha, one of the Algarve's most famous beaches. Arrive early to claim a good spot. Explore the dramatic red sandstone cliffs and sea caves along the beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a kayak or paddleboard at Praia da Rocha (~€10-15/hour) to explore the sea caves and rock formations from the water. Alternatively, join a budget group boat tour from Portimão marina (~€15-20) to see the caves and grottos.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos by bus. Enjoy a quiet evening — visit the Lagos waterfront and watch the fishing boats come in.

meals.breakfast: Toasted sandwich (tosta mista) and coffee at a café in Lagos before departure (~€3-4)
meals.lunch: Beach snack bar at Praia da Rocha — grilled chicken wrap or fresh salad (~€7-10)
meals.dinner: Restaurante O Galeão in Lagos old town — traditional Portuguese bacalhau (salt cod) dishes, prato do dia (~€9-13)

day_by_day.notes: Praia da Rocha is larger and more developed than Lagos beaches but worth a visit for its dramatic cliffs. The group boat tours from Portimão marina are great value and a highlight of the Algarve. Book on the day at the marina for walk-in prices.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recharge day. Sleep in, enjoy a slow breakfast, and do laundry at the hostel. Spend the morning exploring Lagos old town at a leisurely pace — visit the Igreja de Santa Maria, walk the old city walls, and browse local artisan shops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Meia Praia, a long 4km stretch of golden sand east of Lagos (free bus or 20-min walk from the hostel). This is a quieter, less touristy beach perfect for a relaxed afternoon swim and sunbathing.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks at a bar on the Lagos marina. Try a glass of local Algarve wine or a Sagres beer. Explore the evening atmosphere of the old town.

meals.breakfast: Full hostel breakfast if available, or a café near the hostel — scrambled eggs, toast, juice (~€4-6)
meals.lunch: Snack bar at Meia Praia beach — fresh grilled fish sandwich or salad (~€6-9)
meals.dinner: Tasca do Celso in Lagos — a beloved local spot with generous portions of traditional Portuguese food, house wine (~€10-13)

day_by_day.notes: Meia Praia is one of the longest and least crowded beaches near Lagos — ideal for a relaxed day. The walk along the waterfront from Lagos to Meia Praia is scenic and enjoyable. Mid-week is quieter than weekends.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Silves — take the train from Lagos to Tunes then change for Silves (~1 hour total, ~€5-7 return). Visit the impressive Castelo de Silves, a Moorish castle with panoramic views over the Algarve interior (~€3 entry). Explore the charming historic town center.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Silves Cathedral (Sé de Silves, free or small donation) and the Museu Municipal de Arqueologia (~€2). Stroll along the banks of the Arade River. Browse the local market if it's running.
day_by_day.evening: Return by train to Lagos. Enjoy a relaxed evening at the hostel or explore the Lagos bar scene.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and pastel de nata at Lagos train station café before departure (~€2-3)
meals.lunch: Restaurante Marisqueira Rui in Silves — famous for grilled chicken and cataplana, very popular with locals (~€10-14)
meals.dinner: Self-catering or a cheap prego/bifana sandwich from a local snack bar in Lagos (~€4-6)

day_by_day.notes: Silves is one of the most historically significant towns in the Algarve and very budget-friendly. The castle is in excellent condition and offers great views. The train journey through the Algarve countryside is scenic and relaxing. Check train times at CP (Comboios de Portugal) website.

day_by_day.morning: Second wine tasting experience — take a bus toward Lagoa and visit Adega Cooperativa de Lagoa, one of the oldest wine cooperatives in the Algarve. They offer affordable tastings of local Algarve wines including the regional red, white, and rosé varieties (~€5-10 for a tasting flight). Very authentic and local experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the town of Lagoa briefly, then head to nearby Carvoeiro (~15 min by taxi or local bus). Walk the clifftop boardwalk (Percurso dos Sete Vales Suspensos trailhead is nearby) and visit the small but beautiful Praia de Carvoeiro beach.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos by bus (~30-40 min). Enjoy dinner and a nightcap in the old town.

meals.breakfast: Yogurt and fruit from the supermarket or hostel (~€2-3)
meals.lunch: Snack bar in Carvoeiro near the beach — grilled sardines on bread (sardinhas assadas) with a cold beer (~€7-10)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Nah Nah Bah in Lagos — popular burger and craft beer spot, great value (~€9-13)

day_by_day.notes: The Adega Cooperativa de Lagoa is a hidden gem for wine lovers on a budget — far cheaper than private wineries. Call ahead to confirm tasting hours. Carvoeiro is a picturesque fishing village worth a short visit. The clifftop walk near Carvoeiro is free and stunning.

day_by_day.morning: Hike the Rota Vicentina — specifically the Fishermen's Trail (Trilho dos Pescadores) section near Burgau (~15 min bus from Lagos). This coastal trail runs along dramatic clifftops with views of hidden beaches and the Atlantic. Walk from Burgau toward Salema (~7km, 2-3 hours, free).
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Praia de Salema, a beautiful and relatively quiet beach in a small fishing village. Swim, relax, and explore the village. Have lunch at a local restaurant.
day_by_day.evening: Take the bus back to Lagos from Salema (~20 min, ~€2-3). Enjoy a sunset walk along the Lagos waterfront.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and toast at a café in Burgau before starting the hike (~€3-4)
meals.lunch: Restaurante Boia Bar in Salema — fresh grilled fish, local wine, sea views (~€10-14)
meals.dinner: Cheap and cheerful — grab a takeaway piri-piri chicken from Frango Assado near the hostel in Lagos (~€6-8)

day_by_day.notes: The Fishermen's Trail is one of the best free activities in the Algarve. Wear proper walking shoes and bring water and sunscreen. The trail can be uneven in places. September weather is ideal for hiking — not too hot. Download the trail map from the Rota Vicentina website.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the beaches east of Lagos for a change of scenery. Take a bus to Alvor (~20 min, ~€2) and walk the Alvor Estuary boardwalk (free) — a beautiful nature reserve with flamingos, herons, and stunning views over the lagoon and Monchique mountains.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk from the estuary to Praia de Alvor, a wide sandy beach with calm waters — great for swimming. The beach is less crowded than Lagos beaches and has a lovely laid-back vibe. Explore the charming whitewashed village of Alvor.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos by bus. Final evening to explore any remaining spots in Lagos — visit the fort (Forte da Ponta da Bandeira, ~€3) at sunset for great views.

meals.breakfast: Pastelaria in Lagos before departure — coffee, pastel de nata, and orange juice (~€3-4)
meals.lunch: Tasca in Alvor village — prato do dia with soup, main, and drink (~€8-11)
meals.dinner: Restaurante A Forja in Lagos — traditional Algarvian cuisine, generous portions, local wine (~€11-15)

day_by_day.notes: Alvor is a wonderful and underrated destination near Lagos. The estuary boardwalk is free and takes about 45 minutes to walk. Birdwatching is excellent here in September. The village of Alvor has a lovely authentic feel with fewer tourists than Lagos.

day_by_day.morning: Final full beach day — return to your favorite beach from the trip (Ponta da Piedade, Praia do Camilo, or Meia Praia). Spend a leisurely morning swimming and relaxing. Take final photos of the iconic Algarve coastline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Lagos for souvenir shopping and last-minute exploration. Browse the local shops on Rua 25 de Abril for affordable Portuguese souvenirs — local wine bottles (~€5-8), tinned fish (conservas, ~€3-5), ceramic tiles, and cork products. Visit the Lagos market one last time.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Lagos — splurge slightly on your last night for a memorable meal. Try a cataplana (traditional Algarvian seafood or meat stew cooked in a copper pot) at a local restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at the hostel or a café — eggs, toast, juice, coffee (~€5-7)
meals.lunch: Light beach snack — fruit, cheese, bread from the supermarket (~€4-5)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Casinha do Petisco in Lagos — excellent cataplana de marisco or cataplana de porco com amêijoas (pork and clams), local wine (~€14-18 as a farewell splurge)

day_by_day.notes: Tinned fish (conservas) make excellent and affordable Portuguese souvenirs — look for brands like Tricana, Comur, or Bom Petisco. Local Algarve wine is also great value to bring home. Pack any wine bottles carefully in your checked luggage.

day_by_day.morning: Check out of Boutique Taghostel (confirm checkout time — usually 10:00-11:00). Store luggage at the hostel if your bus/transfer is later. Take a final morning walk through Lagos old town and along the waterfront. Grab a last pastel de nata and coffee.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight time, take the Eva/Rede Expressos bus from Lagos bus station to Faro Airport (~1.5-2 hours, ~€6-8). Allow at least 3 hours before your flight for the bus journey and airport check-in. Enjoy the scenic Algarve countryside on the way to the airport.
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Faro Airport. Reflect on 13 wonderful days exploring the beaches, wines, and culture of the Algarve!

meals.breakfast: Final coffee and pastel de nata at a Lagos café (~€2-3)
meals.lunch: Snack at Lagos bus station or a café near the hostel before departure (~€4-6)
meals.dinner: Airport food at Faro Airport if needed — budget for €8-12 at airport prices

day_by_day.notes: Check the bus schedule from Lagos to Faro Airport the day before departure. Buses run several times daily but confirm exact times at the Lagos bus station or online. Allow extra time for the journey in case of delays. Keep €10-15 in cash for any last-minute transport or airport expenses.

trip_options.title: Classic Portugal Algarve Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.location: Rua Dr. Faria e Silva, 32, Lagos, PT (37.1038,-8.6730)

day_by_day.morning: Arrival day — no morning activities scheduled. Flight UA lands at 22:30.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrival day — no afternoon activities scheduled. Travel from Faro Airport to Boutique Taghostel in Lagos (approx. 1 hour by taxi or shuttle, ~€35–45).
day_by_day.evening: Late arrival at Boutique Taghostel. Check in, freshen up, and take a short stroll along the nearby Rua Dr. Faria e Silva to get oriented. Grab a late-night snack or drink at a nearby bar before resting.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in transit
meals.lunch: N/A — in transit or airport dining
meals.dinner: Late-night snack at a local tasca or bar near the hostel — try a bifana (pork sandwich) and a Sagres beer for under €8

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange airport transfer in advance. Boutique Taghostel is centrally located in Lagos old town, making it easy to walk everywhere. Keep luggage light for the check-in walk. Rest well — big days ahead!

day_by_day.morning: Slow start — enjoy breakfast at the hostel or a nearby café. Walk to Praia Dona Ana (15-minute walk from the hostel), one of Lagos's most iconic beaches with golden cliffs and calm turquoise water. Swim, relax, and soak in your first full Algarve morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Lagos old town on foot. Visit the historic Ponta da Bandeira Fort (€3 entry), stroll through the charming Praça Gil Eanes, and browse the local market stalls. Stop at the Igreja de Santo António for a glimpse of stunning azulejo tilework.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Marina de Lagos for a sunset walk. Dine at a waterfront restaurant with fresh grilled fish and local wine.

meals.breakfast: Café Ginginha or similar local café near the hostel — pastel de nata, coffee, and fresh juice (~€5)
meals.lunch: Picnic on Praia Dona Ana — grab bread, local cheese, cured meats, and fruit from a nearby mini-market (~€8)
meals.dinner: O Camilo Restaurant near Praia Dona Ana — grilled sea bass or cataplana de marisco (~€18–25 per person)

day_by_day.notes: September is ideal beach weather in the Algarve — expect 25–28°C and minimal crowds compared to August. Bring sunscreen, a hat, and a reusable water bottle.

day_by_day.morning: Join the Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim experience. Depart from Lagos by local bus or rideshare to Praia da Marinha (approx. 30 minutes east). Hike the dramatic clifftop trail with breathtaking views of golden limestone arches, sea stacks, and hidden coves. The trail is moderate and takes about 2 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend to Praia da Marinha beach for a swim in the crystal-clear water. Explore the small sea caves and rock formations accessible at low tide. Relax on the beach and enjoy the scenery before heading back to Lagos.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos. Enjoy a relaxed evening in the old town — explore the lively Rua 25 de Abril bar street for drinks and tapas-style petiscos.

meals.breakfast: Hostel breakfast or local padaria (bakery) — toast, eggs, and coffee (~€6)
meals.lunch: Pack a lunch from a local deli or grab food at the small beach kiosk near Praia da Marinha (~€10)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Adega da Marina in Lagos — traditional Portuguese cuisine, try the arroz de lingueirão (razor clam rice) (~€15–20 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Check tide times before visiting Praia da Marinha — low tide is best for exploring the caves and rock pools. Wear sturdy sandals or water shoes for the rocky terrain. Bus 78 runs from Lagos to Carvoeiro area; check local schedules.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning trip to Ponta da Piedade, Lagos's most spectacular coastal landmark. Walk the clifftop path and descend the steps to the sea-level viewpoints. Optionally hire a small boat from the base (€10–15) to explore the sea caves and grottos up close.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Meia Praia, a long sandy beach just east of Lagos accessible by a short ferry or taxi. This wide, calm beach is perfect for a relaxed afternoon swim and sunbathing. Rent a sunbed and umbrella (~€8) and unwind.
day_by_day.evening: Back in Lagos, enjoy a wine-focused evening. Visit a local wine bar such as Vinha Bar and sample Algarve regional wines — try a crisp white from the Lagoa DOC or a local rosé.

meals.breakfast: Café Correia near the hostel — fresh orange juice, toast with local honey and butter (~€5)
meals.lunch: Beach bar at Meia Praia — grilled sardines, salad, and a cold beer (~€14)
meals.dinner: Casinha do Petisco in Lagos old town — petiscos (Portuguese tapas) and regional wines (~€18–22 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The ferry to Meia Praia runs from the marina and costs about €1.50 each way — a fun and scenic short crossing. Ponta da Piedade is best visited in the morning before tour groups arrive.

day_by_day.morning: Join the Algarve Wine & Vineyard Tour in the Lagoa DOC wine region (approx. 40 minutes east of Lagos by car or organized tour shuttle). Tour the vineyards, learn about the unique terroir of the Algarve, and discover how local grape varieties like Negra Mole and Crato Branco are cultivated.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the wine tour with guided tastings at two or three local wineries. Sample whites, reds, rosés, and the famous Algarve medronho (arbutus berry spirit). Many wineries offer cheese and charcuterie pairings — a perfect mid-range indulgence.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos in the late afternoon. Enjoy a quiet evening — stroll the old town walls and relax with a glass of wine purchased from the vineyard tour.

meals.breakfast: Hostel breakfast or local café — yogurt, fruit, and coffee (~€6)
meals.lunch: Included as part of the vineyard tour experience — charcuterie, local cheeses, olives, and bread paired with wine
meals.dinner: Restaurante Nah Nah Bah in Lagos — creative burgers and craft beers for a casual, affordable evening (~€12–16 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Algarve Wine & Vineyard Tour in advance, especially in September when harvest season begins. Many tours include round-trip transport from Lagos. Designate a non-drinking companion or use the tour shuttle — do not drive after tastings.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Sagres, the dramatic southwestern tip of Portugal (approx. 30 minutes west of Lagos by bus or car). Visit the imposing Fortaleza de Sagres (€3 entry), a 15th-century fortress perched on a windswept promontory with stunning Atlantic views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Praia do Beliche, a secluded beach near Sagres accessible via a short cliff path — one of the most dramatic and unspoiled beaches in the Algarve. Swim in the cooler Atlantic waters and enjoy the wild, rugged scenery. Alternatively, visit Cabo de São Vicente, the most southwestern point of continental Europe.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos. Enjoy a relaxed dinner and early evening — perhaps pick up a bottle of local wine from a shop and enjoy it on the hostel terrace or rooftop.

meals.breakfast: Local padaria in Lagos before departure — croissant, coffee (~€4)
meals.lunch: A Sagres restaurant near the fortress — fresh tuna steak or grilled octopus salad (~€14–18)
meals.dinner: Tasca do Celso in Lagos — rustic, affordable Portuguese home cooking, try the bacalhau à brás (~€13–17 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Sagres can be windy even in September — bring a light jacket. The Eva bus company runs regular services from Lagos to Sagres. Cabo de São Vicente is just 6 km from Sagres and worth the short detour for the iconic lighthouse and dramatic cliffs.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recharge morning. Sleep in, enjoy a leisurely breakfast, and explore the Lagos Saturday market (Mercado de Lagos) if it falls on a market day. Browse fresh produce, local honey, almonds, figs, and handmade crafts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Praia do Camilo, a small and intimate beach near Lagos accessible via a wooden staircase carved into the cliffs. Swim in the sheltered cove and explore the surrounding rock formations. This is one of the most photogenic beaches near Lagos.
day_by_day.evening: Treat yourself to a slightly elevated dinner experience — a mid-range splurge for the week's midpoint. Enjoy a candlelit dinner with fresh seafood and Algarve wine.

meals.breakfast: Extended hostel breakfast or Café Laranja in Lagos — full Portuguese breakfast with eggs, presunto, cheese, and coffee (~€8)
meals.lunch: Light snack at the beach — fruit, nuts, and a cold drink from a kiosk (~€6)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Dom Sebastião in Lagos — upscale traditional Portuguese cuisine, try the cataplana de peixe (fish stew) (~€25–35 per person, a mid-trip splurge)

day_by_day.notes: Praia do Camilo is a short 10-minute walk from the hostel. It gets busy in the afternoon — arrive by 2pm to secure a good spot. The wooden staircase has 200 steps, so wear comfortable shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Join the Benagil Sea Cave Kayak Tour — one of the Algarve's most iconic experiences. Travel to Benagil (approx. 45 minutes east of Lagos) and paddle through the legendary Benagil Cave, a cathedral-like sea cave with a natural skylight opening. The guided kayak tour typically lasts 2–3 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the kayak tour, relax on Praia de Benagil or nearby Praia de Carvalho, a hidden gem accessible through a short tunnel in the cliffs. Swim, sunbathe, and enjoy the dramatic coastal scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos. Enjoy a casual evening — grab drinks at a rooftop bar and watch the sunset over the Atlantic.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hostel or a local café before departure — toast, eggs, and coffee (~€6)
meals.lunch: Seafood lunch at a restaurant in Carvoeiro village near Benagil — grilled fish of the day and salad (~€15–18)
meals.dinner: O Trovador in Lagos — cozy restaurant with live fado music some evenings, traditional Portuguese dishes (~€16–22 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Benagil Kayak Tour well in advance — it is one of the most popular experiences in the Algarve and fills up quickly. Wear a swimsuit under your clothes and bring a dry bag for your phone and valuables. The cave is only accessible by sea — kayak, paddleboard, or boat tour.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the inland Algarve for a change of scenery. Take a bus or rideshare to Silves (approx. 45 minutes northeast of Lagos), the ancient Moorish capital of the Algarve. Visit the impressive red sandstone Castelo de Silves (€2.80 entry) with panoramic views over the surrounding orange groves.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stroll through Silves old town, visit the Gothic Cathedral, and browse the local shops for handmade ceramics and regional products. Stop at a local quinta (farm) on the way back to Lagos for a tasting of fresh orange juice, local almonds, and carob products.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos. Enjoy a wine and cheese evening — pick up a selection of local wines, queijo de cabra (goat cheese), and presunto from a local deli and enjoy a relaxed evening at the hostel.

meals.breakfast: Local café in Lagos before departure — pastel de nata and galão coffee (~€4)
meals.lunch: Café Inglês in Silves — popular restaurant with a terrace overlooking the castle, try the piri-piri chicken (~€13–16)
meals.dinner: Self-catered wine and cheese evening at the hostel — local wines, cheeses, olives, and bread from a deli (~€15–20 for two)

day_by_day.notes: Silves is a wonderful contrast to the coastal beaches — cooler, quieter, and rich in history. September is also the time of the Silves Medieval Fair (check exact dates), which would be a spectacular bonus if it coincides with your visit. The town is easily walkable.

day_by_day.morning: Beach morning at Praia da Luz, a charming village beach 8 km west of Lagos (accessible by bus or taxi, ~15 minutes). The beach has calm, clear water and a relaxed village atmosphere — perfect for a morning swim and walk along the promenade.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the village of Luz on foot — visit the small Roman ruins and the whitewashed Igreja de Nossa Senhora da Luz. Rent a paddleboard or kayak from the beach (~€15/hour) for an active afternoon on the water.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos for a final evening in the old town. Join a sunset boat tour from the marina (approx. €25–30) for golden hour views of the Lagos coastline and sea caves from the water.

meals.breakfast: Café on the Praia da Luz promenade — fresh fruit salad, yogurt, and coffee (~€7)
meals.lunch: Snack bar on Praia da Luz beach — toasted sandwich, salad, and a cold drink (~€10)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Mullens in Lagos — lively atmosphere, great steaks and seafood, popular with locals and travelers (~€18–24 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Praia da Luz is a quieter, more family-oriented alternative to Lagos beaches — great for a relaxed morning. The sunset boat tour from Lagos Marina is a highlight — book in advance through the marina or your hostel.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Portimão and Praia da Rocha (approx. 20 minutes east of Lagos by train or bus). Praia da Rocha is one of the Algarve's most famous beaches — a wide, golden stretch backed by dramatic ochre cliffs. Spend the morning swimming and exploring the beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Museu de Portimão (free on Sunday afternoons, otherwise €3) — a fascinating museum built inside a former sardine canning factory, telling the story of the Algarve's fishing heritage. Stroll along the Portimão riverside promenade and browse the local shops.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos. Enjoy a final wine tasting evening — visit a local wine shop for a guided tasting of Algarve DOC wines, or join a small group wine tasting event organized through the hostel.

meals.breakfast: Hostel breakfast or local café in Lagos before departure (~€6)
meals.lunch: Taberna da Maré in Portimão — riverside restaurant famous for grilled sardines, a true Algarve classic (~€12–16)
meals.dinner: A Forja in Lagos — beloved local restaurant, try the espetada (meat skewers) or grilled swordfish (~€15–20 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Lagos–Portimão train is cheap (€2.35 one way) and scenic. Praia da Rocha can be busy even in September — arrive early for the best spots. The Portimão sardine festival (Festa da Sardinha) sometimes extends into September — check local event listings.

day_by_day.morning: Final full beach day — revisit your favorite beach from the trip or try Praia do Porto de Mós, a quieter beach west of Lagos with beautiful cliff scenery and calm water. Spend a leisurely morning swimming, reading, and soaking up the last of the Algarve sun.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Lagos for souvenir shopping and last-minute exploration. Pick up local products — Algarve wines, medronho, local honey, almond sweets (Dom Rodrigos), and handmade ceramics. Visit the Mercado de Lagos for fresh produce and local crafts.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner — celebrate the end of a wonderful trip with a special meal. Dress up slightly and enjoy a memorable final evening in Lagos.

meals.breakfast: Slow breakfast at a café near the hostel — full Portuguese breakfast with fresh orange juice (~€8)
meals.lunch: Light beach picnic — local bread, cheese, olives, and fruit from the market (~€8)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Bon Vivant in Lagos — elegant but accessible, excellent seafood and wine list, perfect for a farewell dinner (~€28–38 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Praia do Porto de Mós is a 20-minute walk west from the hostel along the coastal path — a beautiful final morning walk. Pack your souvenirs carefully — wines and spirits need to be in checked luggage. Check hostel checkout time and arrange luggage storage if needed for the last day.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Lagos. Check out of Boutique Taghostel (store luggage if needed). Take one last walk through the old town — visit the Praça da República and the waterfront one final time. Enjoy a slow farewell breakfast at your favorite café.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart Lagos for Faro Airport. Allow at least 1.5–2 hours for the journey (taxi ~€40–50, or bus via Eva Transportes with a connection). Check in for your return flight and browse the airport shops for any last-minute Portuguese wine or pastéis de nata.
day_by_day.evening: Departure. Carry home wonderful memories of the Algarve's golden cliffs, turquoise waters, and exceptional wines.

meals.breakfast: Final pastel de nata and galão at a Lagos café — a perfect last taste of Portugal (~€5)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Faro Airport or a café near the airport (~€10–14)
meals.dinner: In-flight or at destination

day_by_day.notes: Book your airport transfer the night before to avoid stress on departure day. The Eva bus from Lagos to Faro takes approximately 1.5–2 hours with a possible change — allow extra time. Alternatively, a direct taxi or rideshare is more comfortable for the journey with luggage. Confirm your flight details and check-in requirements the evening before.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Portugal Algarve Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Boutique Taghostel
hotel.location: Rua Dr. Faria e Silva, 32, Lagos, PT (37.1038,-8.6730)

experiences.name: Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim
experiences.description: Explore one of the Algarve's most stunning beaches, known for its dramatic golden limestone cliffs, sea caves, and crystal-clear turquoise waters. Hike the clifftop trail from Benagil and descend to the secluded cove for a refreshing swim and snorkeling among the rock formations.

experiences.name: Algarve Wine & Vineyard Tour
experiences.description: Visit local wineries in the Lagoa DOC wine region, the heart of Algarve winemaking. Tour the vineyards, learn about indigenous grape varieties like Negra Mole and Crato Branco, and enjoy guided tastings of crisp whites, rosés, and robust reds paired with local cheeses and charcuterie.

experiences.name: Benagil Sea Cave Kayak Tour
experiences.description: Paddle through the iconic Benagil Cave, one of the world's most photographed sea caves, accessible only by water. A guided kayak tour takes you through hidden grottos, arched rock formations, and secret beaches along the dramatic Algarve coastline, combining adventure with breathtaking natural beauty.

experiences.name: Sagres Sunset Cliffs & Local Seafood Dinner
experiences.description: Visit the windswept Cabo de São Vicente, the southwesternmost point of Europe, for a dramatic Atlantic sunset. Afterward, dine at a traditional tasca in Sagres village, savoring freshly grilled cataplana (seafood stew), percebes (barnacles), and local Algarve wine in an authentic fishing village atmosphere.
experiences.location: Sagres & Cabo de São Vicente, Vila do Bispo

experiences.name: Ria Formosa Natural Park Boat & Oyster Tasting
experiences.description: Take a guided boat tour through the Ria Formosa lagoon system, a protected natural park of tidal channels, barrier islands, and wildlife. Stop at a local oyster farm to taste freshly harvested oysters paired with chilled Algarve white wine, and explore the pristine barrier island beaches accessible only by boat.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Faro Airport at 22:30. Private luxury transfer pre-arranged to Boutique Taghostel in Lagos (~1 hour drive). Check in, unwind with a welcome glass of local Algarve wine left by the hotel, and settle into your room.

meals.breakfast: On flight
meals.lunch: On flight
meals.dinner: Light late-night charcuterie and cheese board from hotel welcome amenity, or a quick bite at the hotel bar if available upon arrival.

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange a private chauffeur transfer from Faro Airport to Lagos. Confirm late check-in with Boutique Taghostel in advance. Keep Day 1 light – rest is the priority after a long flight.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely late breakfast at the hotel, then a gentle orientation walk through the historic old town of Lagos. Explore the charming cobblestone streets, the 15th-century Igreja de Santo António, and the scenic Ponta da Piedade viewpoint with its iconic golden rock formations and turquoise waters.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private boat charter from Lagos Marina for a 3-hour coastal cruise along the dramatic sea caves and grottos of the Lagos coastline. Swim in secluded coves accessible only by sea, with chilled champagne and fresh fruit served on board.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Restaurante Adega da Marina, one of Lagos' most celebrated fine dining spots, known for exceptional fresh seafood and regional Algarve cuisine paired with local wines.

meals.breakfast: Full Portuguese breakfast at the hotel – fresh pastries, local cheeses, cured meats, fruit, and specialty coffee.
meals.lunch: Light snacks and chilled drinks served on the private boat charter.
meals.dinner: Restaurante Adega da Marina – grilled sea bass, cataplana de marisco (seafood stew), and a bottle of Algarve white wine.

day_by_day.notes: Book the private boat charter in advance through the hotel concierge. Ponta da Piedade is best visited in the morning before crowds arrive. Wear comfortable walking shoes for the old town stroll.

day_by_day.morning: Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim – Depart early by private car (~40 min east of Lagos) to explore one of the Algarve's most breathtaking beaches. A guided coastal hike along the clifftop trail reveals dramatic golden limestone arches, sea stacks, and hidden coves. Descend to the beach for a refreshing swim in crystal-clear Atlantic waters.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue along the coastal path to nearby Praia de Benagil for a relaxed afternoon. Hire a stand-up paddleboard or kayak locally to explore the base of the cliffs. Enjoy a long, leisurely lunch at a clifftop restaurant overlooking the sea.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos. Enjoy a sunset cocktail at the hotel terrace, then dinner at a premium Lagos restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before departure.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Restaurante O Litoral in Carvoeiro – fresh grilled fish, local salads, and chilled Vinho Verde.
meals.dinner: No Pátio Restaurant, Lagos – intimate fine dining with modern Portuguese cuisine and an excellent wine list.

day_by_day.notes: Wear sturdy hiking sandals or trail shoes for the coastal path. Bring reef shoes for rocky beach entry at Praia da Marinha. Apply high-SPF sunscreen – September sun in the Algarve remains strong. Private driver recommended for the day.

day_by_day.morning: Benagil Sea Cave Kayak Tour – Depart by private car to Benagil Beach (~45 min east). Join a premium small-group or private guided kayak tour through the world-famous Benagil Cave, paddling through sea arches and hidden grottos. The morning light inside the cave is spectacular. Swim inside the cave's interior beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the kayak tour, relax on Praia de Benagil or nearby Praia de Carvalho. Enjoy a slow afternoon with a beach picnic hamper prepared by the hotel – artisan bread, local cheeses, charcuterie, olives, and chilled rosé.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos. Spa treatment at the hotel or a nearby luxury wellness center. Dinner at a premium Lagos restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at the hotel before departure.
meals.lunch: Luxury picnic hamper on the beach – arranged by hotel concierge with local artisan products and chilled Algarve rosé.
meals.dinner: Casinha do Petisco, Lagos – acclaimed for its creative petiscos (Portuguese tapas) and outstanding local wine selection.

day_by_day.notes: Book the private kayak tour well in advance – Benagil is extremely popular. Morning slots (9:00–10:00 AM) offer the best light inside the cave and fewer crowds. Wear a swimsuit under clothes and bring a dry bag for valuables.

day_by_day.morning: Algarve Wine & Vineyard Tour – Private chauffeured tour to the Lagoa DOC wine region (~30 min east of Lagos), the heart of Algarve winemaking. Visit two premium wineries such as Quinta dos Vales and Adega do Cantor. Guided vineyard walks, barrel room tours, and in-depth tastings of Algarve reds, whites, and the region's distinctive medronho brandy.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the wine tour with a third winery visit and a long, indulgent wine-paired lunch at the estate. Explore the sun-drenched vineyards and learn about the unique terroir of the Algarve's limestone and clay soils.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos in the late afternoon. Freshen up and enjoy a quiet evening stroll along the Lagos waterfront promenade before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely breakfast at the hotel.
meals.lunch: Wine-paired estate lunch at Quinta dos Vales – regional dishes including slow-roasted lamb, local cheeses, and honey-drizzled figs paired with estate wines.
meals.dinner: Restaurante Bon Bon (Carvoeiro, Michelin-starred) – tasting menu showcasing the finest Algarve produce with exceptional wine pairings. Reserve well in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Restaurante Bon Bon holds a Michelin star – reservations must be made weeks in advance. The wine tour is best arranged through the hotel concierge as a fully private experience with a dedicated sommelier guide. Pace wine tastings throughout the day.

day_by_day.morning: Sagres Sunset Cliffs & Cabo de São Vicente – Private car to Sagres (~45 min west of Lagos). Morning visit to the dramatic Cabo de São Vicente, the southwesternmost point of continental Europe. Walk the windswept clifftops with breathtaking Atlantic views. Explore the historic Fortaleza de Sagres, a 15th-century fortress steeped in Age of Discovery history.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Sagres town and its pristine beaches – Praia do Martinhal or Praia de Beliche, both wild and uncrowded. Enjoy a relaxed afternoon swim and sunbathe on these remote Atlantic beaches.
day_by_day.evening: Sagres Sunset Cliffs & Local Seafood Dinner – Return to Cabo de São Vicente for the legendary sunset, one of the most dramatic in Europe. Watch the sun sink into the Atlantic from the clifftop. Dinner at a premium Sagres seafood restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel before departure.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Restaurante Mum's, Sagres – fresh grilled fish, percebes (barnacles), and local seafood with Atlantic views.
meals.dinner: A Sagres – premium seafood dinner featuring freshly caught Atlantic fish, grilled octopus, and local wines, timed after the sunset spectacle.

day_by_day.notes: Bring a light jacket for Cabo de São Vicente – the Atlantic wind can be strong even in September. The sunset at Cabo de São Vicente is one of the most iconic experiences in Portugal – arrive 30–45 minutes before sunset for the best spot.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and leisure morning at the hotel. Enjoy a slow breakfast, then spend the morning at the hotel pool or take a gentle yoga session if offered. Alternatively, explore the Lagos Saturday market (Mercado Municipal) for local produce, fresh fish, and artisan goods.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private sailing experience – charter a luxury catamaran from Lagos Marina for a half-day afternoon sail along the coast. Swim in secluded bays, snorkel over rocky reefs, and enjoy chilled drinks on deck as the crew handles everything.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the catamaran as you sail back into Lagos Marina. Dinner at a premium restaurant in Lagos.

meals.breakfast: Extended leisurely breakfast at the hotel – fresh juices, eggs Benedict, smoked salmon, and local pastries.
meals.lunch: Light lunch on the catamaran – fresh fruit, cheese, charcuterie, and chilled white wine.
meals.dinner: Restaurante Vasco da Gama, Lagos – elegant setting with panoramic marina views, serving premium seafood and Portuguese classics.

day_by_day.notes: Day 7 is intentionally relaxed as a mid-trip recovery day. The catamaran charter can be arranged through the hotel concierge. Afternoon sailing offers beautiful golden light on the cliffs.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Silves – Private car to the historic inland town of Silves (~40 min northeast of Lagos). Visit the magnificent Moorish Castelo de Silves, one of the best-preserved medieval castles in Portugal, with panoramic views over orange groves and the Arade River valley. Explore the charming old town and the Gothic cathedral.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a premium local orange and almond farm near Silves for a private tasting experience of local citrus products, almond sweets, and medronho. Then explore the Silves riverside and browse artisan craft shops.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos. Enjoy a premium spa treatment at the hotel or a nearby luxury spa. Dinner in Lagos.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Restaurante Marisqueira Rui, Silves – legendary seafood restaurant famous for its cataplana and grilled fish, beloved by locals and food critics alike.
meals.dinner: The Grill at a Lagos luxury hotel – premium grilled meats and fish with an extensive Portuguese wine list.

day_by_day.notes: Silves is a wonderful contrast to the coastal experience – the inland Algarve is lush, green, and culturally rich. The Silves Medieval Fair (usually August) may have just ended, but the castle and town are beautiful year-round.

day_by_day.morning: Ria Formosa Natural Park Boat & Oyster Tasting – Private car to Faro (~1.5 hours east). Board a premium guided boat tour through the Ria Formosa lagoon, a UNESCO-protected natural park of tidal channels, barrier islands, and salt marshes. Spot flamingos, herons, and migratory birds. Visit a traditional oyster farm for a hands-on tasting of freshly harvested oysters with local white wine.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the barrier island of Ilha Deserta (Desert Island) – accessible only by boat. Pristine white sand beaches stretching for kilometers with virtually no crowds. Swim in the warm, calm lagoon waters. Lunch at the island's acclaimed restaurant.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Faro. Optional visit to Faro's historic old town (Cidade Velha) and the striking bone chapel (Igreja dos Ossos). Private transfer back to Lagos.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before the drive to Faro.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Restaurante Estaminé on Ilha Deserta – one of Portugal's most unique dining experiences, serving fresh seafood on a deserted island. Reservation essential.
meals.dinner: Dinner in Lagos upon return – Restaurante Adega da Marina for a second visit or a new discovery recommended by the hotel concierge.

day_by_day.notes: This is a full-day excursion – depart by 8:00 AM. Book the Ria Formosa boat tour and Ilha Deserta restaurant reservation well in advance. The oyster tasting is a highlight – pair with a crisp Alentejo white wine.

day_by_day.morning: Second Algarve Wine Experience – Return to the Lagoa wine region for a deeper dive. Visit Quinta da Penina or Herdade dos Pimenteiros for a private morning tasting focused on premium reserve wines and aged vintages. Meet the winemaker for an exclusive behind-the-scenes cellar tour.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the winery, drive to the beautiful Praia de Carvoeiro for a relaxed beach afternoon. Rent a sun lounger and umbrella at a premium beach club. Enjoy the dramatic cliff scenery and calm September sea.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagos. Sunset drinks at a rooftop bar in Lagos old town. Dinner at a premium restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel.
meals.lunch: Wine-paired lunch at the winery estate – seasonal Algarve dishes with reserve wine pairings.
meals.dinner: Restaurante Bon Bon (second visit or alternative Michelin-level experience) – or Dom Sebastião Restaurant, Lagos, for traditional Portuguese fine dining.

day_by_day.notes: The private winemaker session should be arranged in advance through the hotel concierge. September is harvest season in the Algarve – you may be able to witness or participate in the grape harvest, a truly special experience.

day_by_day.morning: Luxury golf morning at Palmares Ocean Living & Golf (~10 min from Lagos) – one of the Algarve's most scenic golf courses with stunning Atlantic and estuary views. Even non-golfers can enjoy the clubhouse, spa, and panoramic terrace. Alternatively, a private surf lesson at Meia Praia beach for those seeking an active morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Praia de Meia Praia – Lagos' longest beach, a sweeping 4km arc of golden sand just minutes from the hotel. Spend a relaxed afternoon at a premium beach club with sun loungers, cocktails, and Atlantic swimming. The September sea temperature is perfect (~22°C).
day_by_day.evening: Farewell-style premium dinner experience – book a private chef dinner or a special tasting menu at one of the Algarve's finest restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel.
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Palmares Golf Clubhouse restaurant – light Mediterranean dishes with panoramic Atlantic views.
meals.dinner: Private chef dinner arranged at the hotel or a premium tasting menu at Restaurante Fortaleza do Guincho (if willing to travel) – one of Portugal's most celebrated fine dining experiences.

day_by_day.notes: Palmares Golf requires advance tee time booking. Meia Praia is easily walkable or a short taxi from the hotel. September is ideal for beach days – warm sun, fewer crowds than peak summer.

day_by_day.morning: Final coastal exploration – Private boat tour to the most secluded sea caves and beaches near Lagos that can only be reached by water. Snorkel over vibrant marine life, explore hidden grottos, and anchor in a private cove for a final Atlantic swim.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Lagos for a leisurely afternoon. Visit the Mercado de Lagos for last-minute artisan souvenirs – local ceramics, cork products, almond sweets, and bottles of Algarve wine to take home. Stroll the marina and enjoy a final coffee at a waterfront café.
day_by_day.evening: Premium farewell dinner at the finest restaurant in Lagos – a celebratory meal to mark the end of an extraordinary trip.

meals.breakfast: Special farewell breakfast at the hotel – request a premium spread with local specialties, fresh pastries, and sparkling wine.
meals.lunch: Light lunch on the boat – fresh seafood, local bread, and chilled Algarve white wine.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Restaurante Bon Bon or Dom Sebastião – multi-course tasting menu with premium wine pairing, celebrating 12 days in the Algarve.

day_by_day.notes: Pack purchased wines carefully for the flight home – wine shipping services are available in Lagos if needed. Confirm checkout time and airport transfer for the following day. Tip hotel staff generously for outstanding service throughout the stay.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Lagos – Enjoy a last leisurely breakfast at the hotel. Take a final walk to Ponta da Piedade for one last look at the iconic golden cliffs and turquoise sea. Pick up any remaining souvenirs in the old town.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Boutique Taghostel. Private luxury transfer to Faro Airport (~1 hour). Depending on flight time, enjoy a final lunch near the airport or in Faro's charming old town.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Faro Airport. Carry memories of 13 extraordinary days in the Algarve – dramatic cliffs, world-class wines, pristine beaches, and the warmth of Portuguese hospitality.

meals.breakfast: Final full Portuguese breakfast at the hotel – savor every last pastry de nata and bica coffee.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Restaurante Faz Gostos, Faro – elegant regional cuisine in a historic townhouse, ideal for a final Algarve meal before departure.
meals.dinner: Airport or in-flight dining.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5 hours before flight departure for the Faro Airport transfer and check-in. Pre-arrange the private airport transfer with the hotel. Consider purchasing a case of Algarve wine (Quinta dos Vales or Adega do Cantor) to ship home as a lasting memory of the trip.

query: Portugal Algarve, $2200, beach holiday with wine tasting, September from London
